clue.text: Spells raft with two C's, all wrong

indicators.note: all wrong says the letters gathered here are thoroughly jumbled into a new order

parts.note: two copies of the letter C

explanation.surface: Someone tries to spell the word raft with two Cs and gets it completely wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spells' looks like the verb about spelling raft, but it is the definition, as in magic spells. RAFT, WITH and CC are rearranged, signalled by 'all wrong'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spells are the stock-in-trade of sorcery, the magic practised by a witch.

clue.text: Bath clerically connected to these water supplies

definitions.text: Bath clerically connected to these water supplies

parts.words: Bath clerically connected to these water supplies
parts.note: the diocese of Bath is paired with a cathedral city whose name also means springs or sources of water

explanation.surface: A spa town's church links with its water sources.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath and Wells is a Church of England diocese, joining the spa city of Bath with the cathedral city of Wells in Somerset.
explanation.definitionFit: Shafts sunk to draw water are the other meaning of the cathedral city's name.

clue.text: Shopkeeper exchanges a piece

parts.note: to trade is to exchange goods
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper swaps one item for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a piece' looks like an item swapped, but is a man, a playing piece in board games.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is, in British usage, someone who runs a shop or delivers goods.

clue.text: Her hero felt all shaky, flat out

indicators.note: shaky letters are unsteady and wobble into a different order

explanation.surface: A woman's hero is trembling and completely exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat out' suggests collapsed, but it means at top speed. 'shaky' rearranges HER HERO FELT ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Going at full tilt, as fast as possible, is the meaning of both phrases.

clue.text: It's cheaper on the car to walk again

definitions.meaning: a remoulded tyre with new tread, cheaper than a new one
to tread a path once more

explanation.surface: A motorist saves money by going on foot once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A remoulded tyre is the noun sense; the verb means to set foot on the same path a second time.

clue.text: The originator of " up and under "

definitions.text: The originator of " up and under "

parts.words: The originator of " up and under "
parts.note: one word meaning both someone who sets something up and to sink or go under

explanation.surface: Asks who first came up with a phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The noun means the person who establishes something, setting it up; the verb means a ship sinking, going under.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who establishes an institution, and a ship that fills and sinks, share the same word.

clue.text: Whence dates are taken in hand.

definitions.text: Whence dates are taken in hand.

parts.words: Whence dates are taken in hand.
parts.note: reads like a diary or appointments being handled, but describes the tree that bears dates and the inner surface of the hand

explanation.surface: A secretary explains where appointments get dealt with.
explanation.definitionFit: The date palm yields dates, and the flat of the hand is what holds things taken in hand.

clue.text: Come up with 'more money

explanation.surface: Get ahead and earn a higher salary.
explanation.definitionFit: To get up or emerge, and read as two words, a pay increase.

clue.text: I and Mona twice suffer obsession

indicators.note: letters that suffer are knocked about and pushed into a new arrangement
twice asks for the name Mona two times over

explanation.surface: Two women named Mona and the narrator are all fixated on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles MONA, and 'suffer' rearranges I with MONA MONA.
explanation.definitionFit: Monomania is a fixation on one single subject.

clue.text: Flowers of the Upper House -

definitions.meaning: a name for the wild arum or cuckoo-pint plant
the peers and peeresses who sit in the House of Lords

explanation.surface: Bouquets in the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: A folk name for the wild arum plant, and the titled members of Britain's second parliamentary chamber.

clue.text: Tract of grassland left untidy

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or piece of grassland in poetic usage

indicators.note: untidy says the letters of the word left lie in disorder and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A stretch of meadow has been left in a scruffy state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tract' looks like a stretch of land to go with grassland, but it is a pamphlet. 'untidy' rearranges LEFT to FLET.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet, especially a religious or political one, much like a handbill.

clue.text: Socially acceptable Head Boy is ideal

parts.note: U means upper-class or socially acceptable, from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U
top is the head of something
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A head boy who behaves properly is a model pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Something utopian belongs to an imagined perfect society, hence idealised.

clue.text: City that's eleven before midweek

parts.note: a football eleven whose club name has a city followed by the midweek day, Wednesday

explanation.surface: A riddle about a city and the middle of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheffield Wednesday is an English football club; an eleven is a football team, and Wednesday is midweek, so the city comes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yorkshire city gives its name to the football club Sheffield Wednesday.

clue.text: Staged, after sunset in late June

definitions.text: Staged, after sunset in late June

parts.words: Staged, after sunset in late June
parts.note: describes a Shakespeare play set on a midsummer night, so staged on a June evening

explanation.surface: An outdoor theatre performance held on a summer evening.
explanation.walkthrough: The reference is Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream: midsummer night falls after sunset in late June.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midsummer Night's Dream is the play, shortened to its last word.

clue.text: Object to medicine-man capturing a bird"

indicators.note: capturing says one piece holds the other prisoner inside it

parts.note: DR, short for doctor, a medicine man
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A tribal healer is reluctant to trap a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' is the verb, to raise an objection, not a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise doubts or protest mildly.

clue.text: 15, for instance, lived up to brave precedent.

indicators.note: precedent means going before, so this piece comes first in the answer

parts.note: to brave something is to dare it

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word lived is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A hero lived up to an example of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LIVED into DEVIL, and 'precedent' puts DARE in front. 15 across is the swashbuckling musketeer recruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The reckless swordsman of Dumas's novel is a fine example of a fearless risk-taker.

clue.text: A grant and new outfit for Him to join the famous three

definitions.text: Him to join the famous three

indicators.note: a new outfit dresses these letters up in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A recruit gets money and fresh clothes on joining a celebrated trio.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous three are Dumas's Three Musketeers, whom the young Gascon joins. 'new outfit' rearranges A GRANT AND.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dumas's novel the young Gascon hero becomes the fourth companion of Athos, Porthos and Aramis.

clue.text: Nearly put the 'feet up all evening

parts.note: nigh means nearly

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the piece beside it is read upwards

explanation.surface: A tired person spends the whole evening resting their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put the ... up' turns FT into TF; 'evening' is the noun, the coming of dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is dusk, the start of evening.

clue.text: They didn't quite win the Fell Race.

definitions.text: They didn't quite win the Fell Race.

parts.words: They didn't quite win the Fell Race.
parts.note: fell running is hill racing; those who finished just behind the winner of any race

explanation.surface: A report on the competitors who narrowly lost a hill race.
explanation.walkthrough: A fell race is a race over hills in northern England, so the entrants literally ran up, as well as finishing second.
explanation.definitionFit: Those placed just behind the winner in a contest, literally running up the fell.

clue.text: Sink: to keep: coal in

definitions.meaning: a container for holding coal by the fire

explanation.surface: A kitchen sink used as a place to store coal.
explanation.definitionFit: To hole a ship deliberately, and the metal bucket that holds fuel by a fireplace.

clue.text: Sir Charles Napier's confession

parts.note: the general reputedly reported his conquest of Sindh with a one-word Latin pun meaning I have sinned

explanation.surface: A Victorian general admits to wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: After taking Sindh in 1843, Napier supposedly sent the Latin for 'I have sinned', punning on 'I have Sindh'; the joke was in fact Punch's.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'I have sinned', the famous one-word admission of guilt.

clue.text: Doctrine of a litter producer

parts.note: a litter of puppies points to the animal
MA, mother, who produces the young

explanation.surface: A creed belonging to a mother dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The producer of a litter of puppies is the dog's ma, the mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a settled set of beliefs laid down as true by an authority.

clue.text: Cultivate sex appeal and a figure

parts.note: to dig the soil is to cultivate it
IT, as in the 1920s 'It girl', means sex appeal

explanation.surface: Develop your allure and keep a good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a figure' sounds like a shapely body after sex appeal, but means a numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is any of the numerals nought to nine.

clue.text: Saw a goblin

definitions.meaning: a dwarfish earth spirit of folklore

explanation.surface: Spotted a goblin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pithy maxim or aphorism, and a small earth spirit guarding underground treasure.

clue.text: Such waters can imperil and -cut her adrift

indicators.note: adrift says these letters float loose and settle in a different order

explanation.surface: Dangerous seas may cut a ship loose and set it drifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adrift' rearranges CUT HER AND; 'can imperil' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Waters not mapped on any chart are a byword for unknown territory.

clue.text: 21's' front and back 'looking gloomy

parts.note: the first letter of the answer to 21 across
the rear is the back

explanation.surface: A figure seen from front and back looks miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 across's front is its first letter, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, meaning dismal.

clue.text: Wild flower absorbing nitrogen.

indicators.note: absorbing says one piece takes the other in, inside itself

parts.note: the violet is a small purple flower
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A wild flower draws nitrogen from the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' looks as if it describes the flower, but it is the definition, meaning furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild and violent both describe uncontrolled, furious behaviour.

clue.text: Inspire a vocal "The girl that I marry"

indicators.note: a vocal is a sung number, so the words are taken as heard rather than as written

parts.note: the song from Annie Get Your Gun, where the girl is Annie, the singer's mate

explanation.surface: A request that a singer perform a well-known love song.
explanation.walkthrough: The Girl That I Marry is from the musical Annie Get Your Gun: the girl is Annie, the singer's future mate, so it is said as 'Annie mate'.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate someone is to give them life and spirit, to stir them up.

clue.text: Remains of a general

definitions.meaning: the sediment left at the bottom of a wine bottle
belonging to Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general

explanation.surface: What is left after a military commander dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs left behind in a cask, and the possessive form of the American Civil War commander Lee.

clue.text: Insurgent runs Alpine, war:

indicators.note: insurgent letters are rebellious, rising up out of their places into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Rebels make a run through the mountains in a campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in: the Peninsular War (1808-14) was fought in Spain and Portugal against Napoleon. 'Insurgent' rearranges RUNS ALPINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Napoleonic campaign in Iberia is known as the Peninsular War, so the word names that war.
